findings.evidence: The roadmap at `RepresentationTheory/CompactGroups/README.md:334` requires `approx_identity_exists` as “a net of nonnegative symmetric kernels whose convolution tends to the identity uniformly on C(G)”; repository grep finds no `approx_identity_exists`, while lines 316–323 choose a kernel depending on `f` and lines 349–353 require the net as hypotheses.
findings.fix: Construct and expose a neighborhood-directed net of mollifiers, with mollifier and shrinking-support properties and convolution convergence for every continuous function, under the roadmap name `approx_identity_exists`.
findings.issue: `tendsto_convolutionCLM_toLp` assumes kernels `k i` and shrinking supports `U i`; no theorem constructs a single net of mollifiers converging uniformly for every `f`, so the canonical `approx_identity_exists` deliverable is absent.

summary: The public API does not expose the roadmap’s named approximate-identity object: it only proves convergence for a pre-existing family and per-function kernel existence.
